specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: reports page: table with Date, Region, Orders and Revenue columns, and a date-range filter
in_scope: A user can download the reports table as a CSV file from the reports page
The header row names the same four columns as the table
non_goals: Changes to the reports table or its filter

criteria.text: Given the reports page with its table, when the user chooses export, then a CSV file downloads whose header row names Date, Region, Orders and Revenue and whose data rows match the table rows.
criteria.check: Integration test of the export; manual step: open the downloaded file and compare it with the table on screen.

criteria.text: Given a date range set in the filter, when the user exports, then the file contains only the rows inside that range.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 1 is answered; then integration test with a fixture spanning two date ranges.

criteria.text: Given a filter that matches no rows, when the user exports, then the result is the one chosen in open question 2.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 2 is answered; negative test.

expected_areas: the data source the page reads its table from

open_questions.question: Does the export contain every row of the report, or only the rows the date filter shows?

options.changes: The export matches the screen; criterion 2 applies.
The export ignores the filter; criterion 2 is dropped.

open_questions.question: What does the user get when no row matches the filter?

options.option: A file with the header row only

actions_now: Write the draft spec and send the two questions to the owner. Criterion 1 may start now; criteria 2 and 3 wait for the answers.

specs.title: Discount at checkout
in_scope: A discount can be applied to an order at checkout
The checkout shows the discount and the reduced total
non_goals: Changes to prices in the catalog

criteria.text: Given a checkout where a discount applies, when the customer reaches the summary, then the discount is shown as its own line and the total equals the subtotal minus the discount.
criteria.check: Blocked until open questions 1 and 2 are answered; then integration test of the total.

criteria.text: Given a customer who is not eligible for the discount, when the customer reaches the summary, then no discount line appears and the total is unchanged.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 2 is answered; negative test.

criteria.text: Given two offers that could both apply, when the customer checks out, then the total follows the rule in open question 3.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 3 is answered; integration test.

criteria.text: Given checkout with no discount applying, when the customer reaches the summary, then the page is identical to the current checkout.
criteria.check: Regression test of the existing checkout.

open_questions.question: How large is the discount, and how is it calculated?

options.changes: Criterion 1 uses a percentage and rounding must be defined.

options.option: Customers who meet a condition to be defined
options.changes: Criterion 2 applies and the condition must be specified.

open_questions.question: Does the discount combine with other offers?

options.option: No, only one offer per order

options.changes: Criterion 3 uses a stacking rule and the order of calculation must be defined.

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version, draft. Prices are a person's decision and no provisional choice is made.

actions_now: Write the draft with the criteria that do not depend on the questions, and send the three pricing questions to the owner. No discount amount, eligibility or stacking rule is chosen; the pricing work waits.

options.option: Time until the page is usable in the browser

specs.title: Theme and language kept across devices
in_scope: A user's theme and language settings are the same on every device the user signs in on
non_goals: The storage design, including table layout; this is the architect's decision
Settings other than theme and language, until the owner names them

criteria.text: Given a user who sets a theme and a language on device A, when the user signs in on device B, then device B shows the same theme and language.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions for one user.

criteria.text: Given a user who changes the theme on device B, when device A is next opened, then device A shows the new theme.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions for one user.

criteria.text: Given a new user who has set no preferences, when the user opens the application, then the defaults in open question 1 apply.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 1 is answered; test with a new account.

open_questions.question: Which values can theme and language take, and what are the defaults?

options.option: The languages the application already supports

actions_now: Write the draft around the behaviour, leave the table design to the architect, and ask the owner for the allowed values and defaults. Criteria 1 and 2 may proceed.

specs.title: Dark mode toggle on the settings page

in_scope: A dark mode toggle on the settings page
The application screens switch theme when the toggle changes
non_goals: Changes to the settings page other than the toggle

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user turns dark mode on, then the application screens show the dark theme.
criteria.check: Manual step: turn the toggle on and open each main screen; expected result is the dark theme on each. Plus UI test of the toggle.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user opens the email templates or the printable invoice view, then they render as set in open question 1.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is set, when the user leaves the application and returns, then the choice is kept as set in open question 2.
criteria.check: Blocked until open question 2 is answered; integration test.

open_questions.question: Does 'the whole app' include the email templates and the printable invoice view?

options.option: No, both stay as they are
